problems.title: Problem A
problems.problem:
Problem A

A1. The pumping station of a town maintains the water supply level at a pressure of $4.3\,\mathrm{atm}$ at the ground floor of a block of flats.

A1.1. Treating the water as an ideal fluid and its speed in the main water-supply pipe as negligible, the speed of the water flowing from a tap on the second floor, if the taps of successive floors are a distance $\mathrm{d} = 4\,\mathrm{m}$ apart and the tap is at height $\mathrm{h} = 0.8\,\mathrm{m}$ above the floor, is:

(a) $20\,\mathrm{m/s}$ (b) $21\,\mathrm{m/s}$ (c) $22\,\mathrm{m/s}$ (d) $23\,\mathrm{m/s}$

i. Choose the correct answer.

ii. Justify your choice.

A1.2. The floor above which water will not run from the tap is the:

(a) 7th (b) 8th (c) 9th (d) 10th

Given: $1\,\mathrm{atm} = 10^5\,\dfrac{N}{m^2}$, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ and $\rho = 10^3\,\dfrac{Kg}{m^3}$.

i. Choose the correct answer.

ii. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

A2. Two conducting rods $\mathrm{A}x_1$ and $\Gamma x_2$ without resistance are placed on a horizontal floor; they are parallel and a distance $\ell$ apart. Their ends, Α and Γ, are joined by a resistance R. A conductor ΚΛ of negligible resistance, mass m and length $\ell$ can slide without friction with its ends in contact with $\mathrm{A}x_1$ and $\Gamma x_2$. The midpoint of the conductor ΚΛ is fixed to one end of a horizontal ideal spring made of insulating material, whose axis is parallel to $\mathrm{A}x_1$ and $\Gamma x_2$. The other end of the spring is fixed to an immovable support, and its spring constant is k. Perpendicular to the plane of the rods there is a vertical uniform magnetic field of magnitude B, pointing downwards.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-1-fig1.png

A2.1. We displace ΚΛ from its equilibrium position by d and release it. During its motion the rod does not lose contact with the conductors $\mathrm{A}x_1$ and $\Gamma x_2$.

The motion that the rod will perform, after it is released, is:

(a) a forced oscillation

(b) a simple harmonic oscillation

(c) a damped oscillation with exponentially decreasing amplitude

(d) a motion during which beats are produced

i. Choose the correct answer.

ii. Justify your choice.

A2.2. During the motion of the conductor, the charge that passes through a cross-section of it is:

(a) $q = 0$ (b) $q = \dfrac{B\cdot\ell\cdot d}{2\cdot R}$ (c) $q = \dfrac{B\cdot\ell\cdot d}{R}$ (d) $q = \dfrac{2\cdot B\cdot\ell\cdot d}{R}$

i. Choose the correct answer.

ii. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

problems.title: Problem B
problems.problem:
Problem B

B1. The rods ΑΒ and ΑΓ are in equilibrium, touching smooth vertical walls and each other at their common end Α on a smooth horizontal floor, forming an angle of $90^\circ$. The rods have masses $m_1$, $m_2$ and lengths $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$ respectively. Given that the section of the contact of the rods is vertical, the distance between the vertical walls is:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-2-fig1.png

(a) $\dfrac{\ell_1\cdot m_1 + \ell_2\cdot m_2}{m_1 + m_2}$ (b) $\dfrac{\ell_1\cdot\sqrt{m_2} + \ell_2\cdot\sqrt{m_1}}{\sqrt{m_1 + m_2}}$

(c) $\dfrac{\ell_1\cdot\sqrt{m_2} - \ell_2\cdot\sqrt{m_1}}{\sqrt{m_1 + m_2}}$ (d) $\dfrac{\ell_1\cdot m_1 - \ell_2\cdot m_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

i. Choose the correct answer.

ii. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

B2. In the installation shown in the figure, slaked lime paste ($\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$) is produced from calcium oxide (CaO) and water ($\mathrm{H_2O}$). The pipe Σ has a constant cross-section of area A.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-2-fig2.png

The water that flows out of the pipe in a time interval Δt will convert n mol of calcium oxide into slaked lime paste. This process is described by the chemical equation:

$$\mathrm{CaO + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2} + Q\uparrow$$

where Q is the heat released by the reaction. If M is the molar mass of water and ρ its density, the speed with which the water leaves the pipe Σ has magnitude:

(a) $\upsilon = \dfrac{n\cdot\rho\cdot\Delta t}{M\cdot A}$ (b) $\upsilon = \dfrac{n\cdot A\cdot\Delta t}{M\cdot\rho}$ (c) $\upsilon = \dfrac{n\cdot M}{\rho\cdot A\cdot\Delta t}$ (d) $\upsilon = \dfrac{n\cdot A\cdot\Delta t}{2\cdot M\cdot\rho}$

i. Choose the correct answer.

ii. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

problems.title: Problem C
problems.problem:
Problem C

C1. Two thin vertical wires Αx and Γy, of negligible resistance, are fixed to an insulating horizontal floor. The two wires are parallel to each other, a distance $\mathrm{L} = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ apart, and are very long. Between the points Η and Θ we connect a source of emf $\mathrm{E} = 6\,\mathrm{V}$ and internal resistance $\mathrm{r} = 1\,\Omega$, and there is also a switch δ. Between the points Κ and Λ, the resistor of the circuit has resistance $\mathrm{R_1} = 10\,\Omega$. The whole arrangement lies inside a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $\mathrm{B} = 2\,\mathrm{T}$ and direction as shown in the figure. The plane of the arrangement is perpendicular to the field lines. We place a conducting rod ΜΝ of mass $\mathrm{m_1} = 0.3\,\mathrm{kg}$, length L and resistance $\mathrm{R_2} = 10\,\Omega$. The rod is fixed to one end of a vertical, massless and inextensible string $\nu_1$. The other end of the string is wound many times around the inner radius $\rho_1 = 0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ of a uniform double pulley, which is fixed at its centre and can rotate without friction. The rod can move without friction on the vertical wires, with its end Μ constantly in contact with the wire Αx and its end Ν constantly in contact with the wire Γy.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-3-fig1.png

On the outer radius $\rho_2 = 0.4\,\mathrm{m}$ of the pulley a second massless and inextensible string $\nu_2$ is wound, the other end of which is wound around the circumference of a uniform disc of mass $m_3$ and radius $\rho_3 = 0.2\,\mathrm{m}$. The disc is on an inclined floor of inclination angle $\varphi = 30^\circ$.

We close the switch, release the system, and observe that the rod, the pulley and the disc are in equilibrium.

(a) Calculate the magnitude of the static friction acting on the disc, as well as its mass.

At time $t = 0$ we cut the strings $\nu_1$ and $\nu_2$ simultaneously and at the same time open the switch.

(b) Calculate the magnitude of the terminal velocity that the rod ΜΝ will acquire.

After the strings are cut, the disc starts to roll without slipping, descending the inclined floor with constant acceleration. The magnitude of the acceleration of the centre of mass of the disc is $\alpha_{cm} = \dfrac{10}{3}\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

(c) Calculate the rate of change of the gravitational potential energy of the disc at the instant when it has rotated through an angle $\theta = 3\,\mathrm{rad}$.

The magnitude of the acceleration due to gravity is $g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. [15 marks]

C2. The long, narrow cylindrical vessel in the figure, of mass $m_\delta = 4\,kg$, contains water of density $\rho = 10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ up to a height $\mathrm{H} = 1.2\,\mathrm{m}$, and stands on a massless support whose lower end is fixed perpendicularly to the end Γ of the horizontal beam ΑΓ, as shown in the figure. The base of the vessel has area $\mathrm{A_\delta} = 50\,\mathrm{cm^2}$. At depth H there is an orifice of area $\mathrm{A_1} = 10\,\mathrm{cm^2}$, which is closed with a plug. The beam has mass $\mathrm{M} = 20\,\mathrm{kg}$ and length L; it is hinged at the end Α to a vertical wall but is also supported at the point Ν from the ceiling by a vertical string, massless and inextensible. The distance of the point Ν from the point Α is $\mathrm{AN} = \dfrac{3\cdot L}{4}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-3-fig2.png

The magnitude of the acceleration due to gravity is $g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

C2.1. Calculate:

(a) The tension of the string.

(b) The magnitude F of the force exerted on the rod by the wall.

C2.2. At time $t_0 = 0$ we pull the plug out abruptly and at time $t_1 = 2.4\,\mathrm{s}$ we put it back instantaneously. Calculate, from time $t_1$ onwards, the tension of the string and the force exerted on the beam by the wall. Treat the water as an ideal fluid. [15 marks]

problems.title: Problem D. Experimental problem: study of the SHM of a mass–spring system
problems.problem:
Problem D. Experimental problem: study of the SHM of a mass–spring system

FIELD OF INVESTIGATION:

1. Excitation of a mass–spring system to perform SHM.

2. Investigation of the relation between the characteristic quantities of the oscillating system and those of SHM.

3. Taking measurements in order to calculate the value of the spring constant k and of the mass $m_\varepsilon$ of the spring, and to verify the validity of the principle of conservation of energy.

PREREQUISITE KNOWLEDGE:

A uniform metal cylinder of mass m attached to the free end of a spring can be set in motion after an additional extension or compression of the spring is produced; the spring is suspended from a fixed point with its axis vertical.

Ignoring every other force except the weight of the body and the elastic force of the spring, we can show that the motion of the body is described by the equation $x(t) = \mathrm{A}\sin(\omega t + \varphi)$ (1), which also identifies the motion as SHM with angular frequency ω and period

$$T = 2\cdot\pi\cdot\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{K}} \qquad (2)$$

The periodicity of SHM is ensured by the fact that when the time is increased by $\dfrac{2\cdot\lambda\cdot\pi}{\omega}$ (λ a natural number), (1) does not change form, since:

$x\left(t + \dfrac{2\lambda\pi}{\omega}\right) = \mathrm{A}\sin\left\{\omega\left(t + \dfrac{2\lambda\pi}{\omega}\right) + \varphi\right\} = \mathrm{A}\sin(\omega t + 2\lambda\pi + \varphi) = \mathrm{A}\sin(\omega t + \varphi)$.

Relation (2) holds in the case of a massless spring (ideal spring). In practice, however, and as a rule, the mass of the spring $m_\varepsilon$ is of the same order of magnitude as the mass m of the body, so if it is not ignored it will appear in the expression for the period.

It can be shown that: $T = 2\cdot\pi\cdot\sqrt{\dfrac{m + \dfrac{m_\varepsilon}{3}}{k}}$ or $T^2 = \dfrac{4\cdot\pi^2}{k}\cdot m + \dfrac{4\cdot\pi^2}{3\cdot k}\cdot m_\varepsilon$, i.e. the equation $T^2 = f(m)$ is linear, of the form $\mathbf{T^2 = a.m + b}$, if we set $\mathbf{a} = \dfrac{\mathbf{4\pi^2}}{\mathbf{k}}$ (slope of the straight line) and $\mathbf{b} = \dfrac{\mathbf{4\pi^2}}{\mathbf{3k}}\,\mathbf{m_\varepsilon}$ (point of intersection with the $T^2$ axis).

We can therefore measure the period T of the oscillations of the system for different values of the mass m and, from the graph, calculate the values of the characteristics k and $m_\varepsilon$ of the spring.

EXPERIMENTAL PART

We experiment with an arrangement that includes a vertical spring suspended from a fixed point, with the possibility of hanging different masses on its free end. When the system is excited, and for a short time interval it is considered to perform SHM, the position of the mass as it moves along the vertical axis can be detected by a transmitter–position (distance) sensor placed below the mass, on the axis of its motion.

The transmitter locates the position x of the oscillating mass at every instant t and sends the data to a computer, where, after their collection and analysis by special software, the graph $x = f(t) = \mathrm{A}\sin(\omega t + \varphi)$ is displayed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-4-fig1.jpg

Each time a different mass m is used, which is set into SHM of amplitude about $20\,\mathrm{cm}$, so that from the corresponding graph the period is calculated as the time difference $t_2 - t_1$ between two successive peaks of the x–t curve.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-4-fig2.png

Image 1: m = 0.4 Kg

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-4-fig3.png

Image 2: m = 0.5 Kg

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-4-fig4.png

Image 3: m = 0.6 Kg

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-4-fig5.png

Image 4: m = 0.7 Kg

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-4-fig6.png

Image 5: m = 0.8 Kg

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2021-4-fig7.png

Image 6: m = 0.9 Kg

The results are recorded in Table «A»:

TABLE «A»

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c} \text{No.} & m\ (\mathrm{Kg}) & t_1\ (\mathrm{s}) & t_2\ (\mathrm{s}) & T = t_2 - t_1\ (\mathrm{s}) & T^2\ (\mathrm{s^2}) \\ \hline 1. & 0.4 & & & & \\ 2. & 0.5 & & & & \\ 3. & 0.6 & & & & \\ 4. & 0.7 & & & & \\ 5. & 0.8 & & & & \\ 6. & 0.9 & & & & \end{array}$$

D1. Calculate the period T that corresponds to each mass and its square $T^2$ (the period T to be calculated to two significant figures and $T^2$ to four).

D2. Draw the graph $T^2 = f(m)$. What is its shape and why? Find its slope a and from it calculate the spring constant k of the spring.

D3. If the theoretical value of the spring constant is $k = 25\,\mathrm{N/m}$, calculate the absolute error Δk and the relative error (Δk)% of the measurement.

D4. From the graph, determine the point of intersection of the graph with the $T^2$ axis and from the value of b calculate the mass $m_\varepsilon$ of the spring.

D5. If the mass of the spring was determined by weighing to be $m_\varepsilon = 300\,\mathrm{g}$, calculate the absolute error $\Delta m_\varepsilon$ and the relative error $(\Delta m_\varepsilon)\%$ of the measurement.

D6. With the method of «least squares», the determination of the coefficients a and b of the linear equation $T^2 = f(m)$ is attempted in a more accurate way than that of the approximate drawing of the graph. This is achieved from the sums in the last row of Table «B», which you will fill in. Given:

$$\alpha' = \dfrac{\mathrm{N}\cdot\sum m\cdot T^2 - \sum m\cdot\sum T^2}{N\cdot\sum m^2 - \left(\sum m\right)^2} \qquad b' = \dfrac{\sum m^2\cdot\sum T^2 - \sum (T^2\cdot m)\cdot\sum m}{N\cdot\sum m^2 - \left(\sum m\right)^2}$$

TABLE «B»

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} \text{No.} & m\ (\mathrm{Kg}) & T^2\ (\mathrm{s^2}) & m^2\ (\mathrm{kg^2}) & T^2\cdot m\ (\mathrm{kg\cdot s^2}) \\ \hline 1. & 0.4 & & & \\ 2. & 0.5 & & & \\ 3. & 0.6 & & & \\ 4. & 0.7 & & & \\ 5. & 0.8 & & & \\ 6. & 0.9 & & & \\ \hline \text{TOTALS} & \sum m_i = & \sum m_i^2 = & \sum T_i^2 = & \sum (T_i^2\cdot m_i) \end{array}$$

D7. From the values of the coefficients a΄ and b΄, calculate the spring constant k and the mass $m_\varepsilon$ of the spring, as well as the corresponding values of the absolute and relative errors with respect to their theoretical values.

[4+4+4+4+4+5+5 marks]

problems.title: Problem A
problems.problem:
Problem A

A1. When a body is in equilibrium at the lower end of a vertical ideal spring of spring constant $k$, whose upper end is fixed to an immovable point, the extension of the spring is $\Delta\ell$. We place the spring–body system on a smooth horizontal plane $(\Pi_1)$ and the body performs simple harmonic oscillation of amplitude $\mathrm{A}$ with restoring constant $D = k$. At some instant, as the body passes through the position of natural length of the spring, it detaches from the spring and continues to move on the horizontal plane. It then enters the convex surface of a smooth quarter-circle of radius $R$ and loses contact with it at a height $h$ above the horizontal floor $(\Pi_2)$. The following relation holds:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-1-fig1.png

(a) $h = \dfrac{\mathrm{A}^2 + 3R\Delta\ell}{3\Delta\ell}$

(b) $h = \dfrac{\mathrm{A}^2 + 2R\Delta\ell}{3\Delta\ell}$

(c) $h = \dfrac{\mathrm{A}^2 + R\Delta\ell}{3\Delta\ell}$

(d) $h = \dfrac{3\mathrm{A}^2 + R\Delta\ell}{3\Delta\ell}$

i. Which is the correct answer? [2 marks]

ii. Justify your answer. [10 marks]

A2. A cylinder of mass $m$ and radius $R = 80\,\mathrm{cm}$ rotates with angular velocity of magnitude $\omega_o = \dfrac{150}{13}\,\mathrm{r/s}$ and is placed so that it comes into contact with a vertical wall and a horizontal floor simultaneously at time $t_o = 0$. The cylinder has the same coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu = 0.2$ with both the wall and the floor, with which it is constantly in contact. The acceleration due to gravity is $g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ and the moment of inertia of the cylinder about its centre of mass is $\mathrm{I}_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{2}mR^2$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-1-fig2.png

A2.A. The cylinder will come to rest at time

(a) $t_1 = 1.2\,\mathrm{s}$ (b) $t_1 = 1.4\,\mathrm{s}$ (c) $t_1 = 1.8\,\mathrm{s}$ (d) $t_1 = 2\,\mathrm{s}$

i. Which is the correct answer? [1 mark]

ii. Justify your answer. [5 marks]

A2.B. If the mass of the cylinder is $m = 6760\,\mathrm{g}$, then the heat released to the surroundings because of the contact of the cylinder with the vertical wall, from time $t_o = 0$ to time $t_1$, is equal to

(a) $24\,\mathrm{J}$ (b) $48\,\mathrm{J}$ (c) $120\,\mathrm{J}$ (d) $144\,\mathrm{J}$

i. Which is the correct answer? [1 mark]

ii. Justify your answer. [6 marks]

Problem B

B1. Two identical smooth flat discs (A) and (B) move on the same horizontal plane towards each other, so that their velocities $\vec{\upsilon}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\vec{\upsilon}_B$ respectively have directions parallel to the horizontal axis $x'x$, as shown in the figure. The velocities have magnitudes $\upsilon_{\mathrm{A}} = 2\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $\upsilon_B = \dfrac{2\cdot\sqrt{3}}{3}\,\mathrm{m/s}$. The discs collide elastically, and at the instant of the collision the straight line joining their centres makes an angle of $150^\circ$ with the axis $x'x$. It is given that $\sin 30^\circ = \cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $\sin 60^\circ = \cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\sin 45^\circ = \cos 45^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$. Calculate the angle that the velocity of disc (A) will make with the axis $x'x$ after the collision. [8 marks]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-2-fig1.png

B2. Inside a vessel standing on a horizontal plane, two ideal liquids that do not mix are at rest. The upper surface of liquid $(Y_1)$ is at height $h$ above the base of the vessel, and this liquid has density $\rho_1$. Above liquid $(Y_1)$ is liquid $(Y_2)$, whose free surface is at height $2\cdot h$ above the base of the vessel and is in contact with the atmospheric air. The density of liquid $(Y_2)$ is equal to $\rho_2$. For the densities, $\rho_1 = 2\rho_2$. At two points A and B of the wall, which lie on the same vertical line, there are two small openings, which are in contact with the atmospheric air. Opening A is at height $x_1$ above the base of the vessel $(x_1 \le h)$ and opening B is at height $x_2$ above the upper surface of liquid $(Y_1)$, for which $x_2 < h$. Liquid spurts out of the two openings and falls at the same point Γ of the horizontal plane. Air resistance is assumed negligible.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-2-fig2.png

B2.A. Calculate the minimum value that the height $x_2$ can take, as a function of the height $h$. [9 marks]

B2.B. Calculate the maximum value that the height $x_2$ can take, as a function of the height $h$. [8 marks]

Problem C

The arrangement in the figure is given, which lies inside a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $B = 2\,\mathrm{T}$, with direction perpendicular to the horizontal plane (Π) of the figure, pointing from the reader into the plane (Π). The arrangement consists of:

• the conductor ΟΓ in the shape of a quarter-circle of radius $\ell = 1\,\mathrm{m}$, of negligible ohmic resistance
• the straight conductor ΟΑ of negligible ohmic resistance
• the straight conductor ΓΔ of negligible ohmic resistance, which is parallel to ΟΑ at a distance $\ell = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ from it.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-3-fig1.png

The ends Α and Δ of the conductors ΓΔ and ΟΑ are conductively connected through a resistor of resistance $R = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\,\Omega$. The conductors ΟΓ and ΟΑ are not connected at the point Ο. A uniform thin conducting rod ΗΖ of ohmic resistance $R_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\,\Omega$ and length $\ell = (\mathrm{HZ}) = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ moves in the plane (Π) parallel to itself, always remaining perpendicular to the conductor ΟΑ. Its end Η is always in contact with the conductor ΟΑ. During its motion the rod is also constantly in contact with the conductor ΟΓ or the conductor ΓΔ. Initially the rod is at rest, with its end Η at the point Ο. At time $t_o = 0$ we apply a force $\vec{F}$ at the midpoint of the rod, in a direction parallel to ΟΑ, so that it starts to move in such a way that its point of contact with the conductor ΟΓ has a constant angular velocity of magnitude $\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\,\mathrm{r/s}$. The rod reaches the point Γ at time $t_1$ with velocity $\vec{\upsilon}_1$ and continues to move with this velocity until it reaches the points Α and Δ.

C1. If the heat released during the motion of the rod ΗΖ while it is in contact with the conductor ΓΔ is equal to $Q = 2\,\mathrm{J}$, calculate the length (ΓΔ). [8 marks]

C2. At time $t_2 = \dfrac{1}{3}\,\mathrm{s}$, calculate the induced emf in the part of the rod through which electric current flows. [8 marks]

C3. At time $t_2 = \dfrac{1}{3}\,\mathrm{s}$, calculate the electric current flowing in the circuit, as well as the power of the Laplace force. [9 marks]

Given: $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

problems.title: Problem D. Study of the electromagnetic force on a current-carrying conductor
problems.problem:
Problem D. Study of the electromagnetic force on a current-carrying conductor

EXPERIMENTAL PART

THEORY

Consider a straight conductor of length L carrying an electric current I. If the conductor is placed in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ with its direction perpendicular to the field lines, an electromagnetic force is expected to be exerted on it, as the resultant of the forces exerted by the magnetic field on the moving electric charges.

Suppose that carriers (e.g. free electrons), each with electric charge q, moving with velocity $\upsilon$, travel the length of the conductor in time Δt; then: $L = \upsilon\cdot\Delta t$ and $\sum q = I\,\Delta t$, therefore $L = \upsilon\dfrac{\sum q}{I}$ or $\sum q\cdot\upsilon = L\cdot I$ (1).

The electromagnetic (Lorentz) force exerted by a magnetic field on an electric charge moving perpendicular to its field lines is given by the relation $F = B\upsilon q$; therefore the corresponding macroscopic force on the conductor, because of (1), will have magnitude $F_L = \sum F = B\upsilon\sum q = BIL$ and is known as the Laplace force.

EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE

The determination of the characteristics of the Laplace force is attempted with the experimental procedure described here.

An electric circuit is set up, as shown in the figure, which includes as power supply a source of constant (DC) voltage 24 V in series with a rheostat, through which the current can be varied. Connected in series in the circuit is a straight conductor (a wire), which passes, without touching, between the poles of a horseshoe magnet placed on the pan of an electronic balance. The direction of the conductor is perpendicular to the field lines of the uniform magnetic field.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-4-fig1.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-4-fig2.png

Initially the circuit is open, so the reading of the balance, which is the normal force $\mathrm{N}_o$, is equal to the weight of the magnet $W_o = m_o g$, and is therefore proportional to its mass $m_o$. If we close the switch, depending on the polarity of the source and hence on the direction of the electric current in the conductor, the reading of the balance will change, showing an "apparent" weight $W$, which will be equal to the new normal force $\mathrm{N} = W_o \pm F_L'$, where $F_L'$ is the electromagnetic force exerted by the straight current-carrying conductor on the magnet. In essence, the magnitude of this force, which is added to or subtracted from the weight of the magnet, is equal to the magnitude of the force $F_L$ exerted by the magnet on the current-carrying conductor, as an action–reaction pair. The aim of the experiment is to take measurements for various values of the length of the conductor that lies inside the magnetic field and of the electric current, in order to relate the magnitude of the force $F_L$ to the length $L$ of the conductor and the current I flowing through it.

TAKING MEASUREMENTS

To simplify the calculations, let us take the directions of the field lines and of the current as in the figure, so that the magnitude of the force $F_L$ is added to the weight $W_o$ of the magnet, and therefore the reading of the balance increases. Let us note here that the balance measures force, but is calibrated so that its reading equals the mass.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2022-4-fig3.png

With the switch open we note the reading of the balance, $m_o = 260\,\mathrm{g}$, which corresponds to the weight of the magnet $W_o = m_o g = 260\cdot10^{-3}\cdot 9.81\,\mathrm{N} = 2.55\,\mathrm{N}$.

We close the switch and adjust so that the current has the value $I = 1\,\mathrm{A}$ for each value of the length of the conductor, from $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $10\,\mathrm{cm}$, that we choose each time to lie inside the magnetic field. For each value of this length we note the reading of the balance and record the results in Table 1:

TABLE 1

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Conductor} & \text{Length } L\ (\mathrm{cm}) & \text{Current } I\ (\mathrm{A}) & \text{Balance reading } m\ (\mathrm{g}) \\ \hline \mathrm{L1} & 1 & 1 & 260.102 \\ \mathrm{L2} & 2 & 1 & 260.205 \\ \mathrm{L3} & 3 & 1 & 260.307 \\ \mathrm{L4} & 4 & 1 & 260.407 \\ \mathrm{L5} & 5 & 1 & 260.510 \\ \mathrm{L6} & 6 & 1 & 260.612 \\ \mathrm{L7} & 7 & 1 & 260.715 \\ \mathrm{L8} & 8 & 1 & 260.817 \\ \mathrm{L9} & 9 & 1 & 260.918 \\ \mathrm{L10} & 10 & 1 & 261.020 \end{array}$$

We repeat the measurement procedure, choosing a particular fixed length of the conductor $L = 4.0\,\mathrm{cm}$ and adjusting so that the current I takes various values from $0.2\,\mathrm{A}$ to $2\,\mathrm{A}$. For each value of the current we note the reading of the balance and record the results in Table 2:

TABLE 2

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Conductor} & \text{Current } I\ (\mathrm{A}) & \text{Length } (\mathrm{cm}) & \text{Balance reading } (\mathrm{g}) \\ \hline \mathrm{I1} & 0.2 & 4 & 260.082 \\ \mathrm{I2} & 0.4 & 4 & 260.164 \\ \mathrm{I3} & 0.6 & 4 & 260.245 \\ \mathrm{I4} & 0.8 & 4 & 260.325 \\ \mathrm{I5} & 1.0 & 4 & 260.408 \\ \mathrm{I6} & 1.2 & 4 & 260.490 \\ \mathrm{I7} & 1.4 & 4 & 260.571 \\ \mathrm{I8} & 1.6 & 4 & 260.652 \\ \mathrm{I9} & 1.8 & 4 & 260.734 \\ \mathrm{I10} & 2.0 & 4 & 260.815 \end{array}$$

PROCESSING THE MEASUREMENTS

For each "reading" $m$ of the balance, because of equilibrium, $\mathrm{N} = W_o + F_L$ or $mg = m_o g + F_L$ or $(m - m_o)g = F_L$ or $F_L = \Delta m\cdot g$.

D1. From the measurements of Table 1, fill in the entries of Table 3. [4 marks]

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Conductor} & I\ (\mathrm{A}) & L\ (\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{m}) & m_0\ (\mathrm{g}) & m\ (\mathrm{g}) & \Delta m\ (\mathrm{g}) & F_L\ (\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{N}) \\ \hline \mathrm{L1} & 1 & 1 & 260 & 260.102 & & \\ \mathrm{L2} & 1 & 2 & 260 & 260.205 & & \\ \mathrm{L3} & 1 & 3 & 260 & 260.307 & & \\ \mathrm{L4} & 1 & 4 & 260 & 260.407 & & \\ \mathrm{L5} & 1 & 5 & 260 & 260.510 & & \\ \mathrm{L6} & 1 & 6 & 260 & 260.612 & & \\ \mathrm{L7} & 1 & 7 & 260 & 260.715 & & \\ \mathrm{L8} & 1 & 8 & 260 & 260.817 & & \\ \mathrm{L9} & 1 & 9 & 260 & 260.918 & & \\ \mathrm{L10} & 1 & 10 & 260 & 261.020 & & \end{array}$$

D2. On a system of rectangular axes, plot the graph of the force (axis $y'y$) against the length $L$ of the conductor (axis $x'x$), determining the points from the data of Table 3. What is the conclusion from the shape of the graph? [3 marks]

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

An ideal massless spring of constant k with natural length $L$ is vertical, with its upper end fixed at an immovable point. A small body (Σ) of mass m hangs from the lower end of the spring and is at rest, while the spring has an extension equal to $d$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2023-1-fig1.png

Next, we place the spring–body system in a smooth vertical quarter circle ΑΓ of radius $R=L$ and centre K, so that its axis is horizontal and coincides with the horizontal radius of the quarter circle. The small body (Σ) touches the upper end Α of the quarter circle, while remaining joined to one end of the spring. The other end of the spring is connected to the centre K of the quarter circle in such a way that the spring–body system can rotate without friction. We release the body (Σ) from the end Α, free to move. The body (Σ) passes through the lower end Γ of the quarter circle and continues to move on a smooth horizontal plane, without ever losing contact with it. The body (Σ) stops momentarily after travelling a distance x on the horizontal plane. The distance x is equal to

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2023-1-fig2.png

(a) $\sqrt{L\cdot(d+\sqrt{2\cdot L\cdot d})}$

(b) $\sqrt{2\cdot L\cdot(d+\sqrt{2\cdot L\cdot d})}$

(c) $\sqrt{L\cdot(2\cdot d+\sqrt{2\cdot L\cdot d})}$

(d) $\sqrt{2\cdot L\cdot(2\cdot d+\sqrt{2\cdot L\cdot d})}$

A. Choose the correct answer. [2 marks]

B. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
Problem 2

In the microcosm there are many small particles, which we call elementary particles. Apart from the well-known ones (proton, electron, neutron, photon), the rest live for a very short time interval. Consequently, they decay quickly (spontaneously) and form other particles. There are detectors, which we have built at research centres in order to study them, in which we can distinguish the trajectories of the charged particles inside a homogeneous magnetic field. The neutral particles we can distinguish indirectly, from the processing of the data of the charged particles.

Suppose that in a detector we see the decay:

$$\mathrm{K}^o\rightarrow\pi^{+}+e^{-}+\ldots$$

that is, the decay of the neutral kaon $\mathrm{K}^o$ into a positively charged pion $\pi^{+}$ and an electron $e^{-}$. The dots indicate that there may also be other particles which, if they are neutral, we do not see in the detector. The trajectories of the particles are perpendicular to the field lines of a homogeneous magnetic field of intensity $\vec{B}$ with direction from the page towards the reader, whose cross-section is a square ΑΓΔΕ of side $\dfrac{5\alpha}{4}$, where $\alpha$ is a constant length. The particle $\mathrm{K}^o$ was created at the point Z and decayed at the point Η (we do not see its trajectory because it is uncharged). The point Η is at a distance $\dfrac{\alpha}{4}$ from the two sides ΔΕ and ΕΑ. The straight segment ΖΗ is parallel to the side ΕΑ. The figure shows the two trajectories (1) and (2) of the two particles produced by the decay of the kaon. The velocity $\vec{\upsilon}_1$ of one particle has the direction ΖΗ, while the velocity $\vec{\upsilon}_2$ of the other particle makes an angle $\varphi=60^o$ with the velocity $\vec{\upsilon}_1$, as shown in the figure. The particle of trajectory (1) leaves from the vertex Γ with velocity perpendicular to the side ΓΔ.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2023-2-fig1.png

(a) Which trajectory corresponds to the pion and which to the electron? Justify your answer. [5 marks]

(b) Someone might claim that in this decay the principle of conservation of momentum is violated. On what experimental data is such a claim based? Give him a logical argument, based on the experiment we perform, which shows that the conservation of momentum is not violated. [5 marks]

(c) The particle of trajectory (2) leaves the magnetic field from a point Λ. Calculate the distance ΗΛ as a function of the length $\alpha$. [5 marks]

(d) If $t_\pi$ and $t_e$ are the times of motion of the pion and of the electron respectively in the magnetic field, find the ratio $\dfrac{t_\pi}{t_e}$. [5 marks]

We consider the weights of the particles negligible. The mass of the pion is 264 times greater than the mass of the electron. The magnitude of the velocity of the electron is 132 times greater than the magnitude of the velocity of the pion. The charge of the pion has the same magnitude as the charge of the electron $\left(q_e=-q_\pi=-e\right)$.

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

A point body of mass $\mathrm{m}=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ is connected to the end of an ideal spring of constant $\mathrm{k}=4\cdot\pi^2\,\mathrm{N/m}$. The system, under the action of a driver, performs a forced oscillation. The driver supplies energy to the system 4 times every 2 seconds. The ratio of the maximum kinetic energy $\mathrm{K_{max}}$ of the body to the maximum potential energy $\mathrm{U_{max}}$ of the oscillation is:

(a) $1$ (b) $2$ (c) $4$ (d) $\dfrac{1}{4}$

A. Choose the correct answer. [2 marks]

B. Justify your choice. [8 marks]

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

The homogeneous wheel of the adjacent figure has radius $R=2\,m$ and rolls without slipping. Let A be a point of the wheel which is at a distance $r=1\,m$ above the centre of mass of the wheel and on the same vertical line as it. The wheel starts at time $t=0$, with no initial velocity, accelerating with an acceleration of magnitude $a_{cm}=2\,m/s^2$. The magnitude of the acceleration of the point A at time $t=1\,s$ is:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2023-4-fig1.png

(a) $\sqrt{2}\,m/s^2$ (b) $\sqrt{3}\,m/s^2$ (c) $\sqrt{5}\,m/s^2$ (d) $\sqrt{10}\,m/s^2$

A. Choose the correct answer. [2 marks]

B. Justify your choice. [8 marks]

problems.title: Problem 5
problems.problem:
Problem 5

A homogeneous vertical rectangular door has a width $\ell$ four times its height $d$ and is supported by hinges at its two ends on a vertical wall. The direction of the force from the lower hinge passes through the midpoint of its upper side. The ratio of the magnitudes of the forces exerted by the upper and the lower hinge respectively is:

(a) $\sqrt{5}$ (b) $2\sqrt{5}$ (c) $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{5}$ (d) $\dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}$

A. Choose the correct answer. [2 marks]

B. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

problems.title: Problem 6
problems.problem:
Problem 6

A homogeneous beam of length $\ell$ and weight w is in limiting equilibrium between two vertical walls, one of which is smooth, while with the other there is friction at their point of contact, with coefficient μ. The distance between the walls is equal to:

(a) $\dfrac{\ell}{\sqrt{\mu^2+4}}$ (b) $\dfrac{2\ell}{\sqrt{\mu^2+4}}$ (c) $\dfrac{\ell}{\sqrt{\mu^2-4}}$ (d) $\dfrac{2\ell}{\sqrt{\mu^2-4}}$

A. Choose the correct answer. [2 marks]

B. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

problems.title: Problem 7
problems.problem:
Problem 7

The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of a circular current-carrying conductor of radius r carrying a current $I_1=10\,mA$ is $B_1$. An electric charge $q=50\,\mathrm{\mu C}$ moves with frequency f on a circular path of radius r, at the centre of which the magnitude of the magnetic field is $B_2=2B_1$. The frequency of rotation of the electric charge is:

(a) $100\,\mathrm{Hz}$ (b) $200\,\mathrm{Hz}$ (c) $400\,\mathrm{Hz}$ (d) $1000\,\mathrm{Hz}$

A. Choose the correct answer. [2 marks]

B. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

problems.title: Problem 8
problems.problem:
Problem 8

On a glass, non-elastic table, the bodies $\Sigma_2$ and $\Sigma_3$, with masses $m_2$ and $m_3$ respectively, are in equilibrium, tied to an ideal spring of constant k. The breaking limit of the table is $T_\theta$. From a height h we release a sphere of mass $m_1$, which collides centrally, elastically and instantaneously with the body $\Sigma_2$. We do not want the table to break, but we also do not want the body $\Sigma_3$ to lose contact with the table. Given are the magnitude of the acceleration of gravity g, $m_1=m$, $m_2=3m$, $m_3=3m$ and $T_\theta=12mg$. The maximum height h for which both constraints are satisfied is:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2023-8-fig1.png

(a) $\dfrac{12mg}{k}$ (b) $\dfrac{24mg}{k}$ (c) $\dfrac{36mg}{k}$ (d) $\dfrac{48mg}{k}$

A. Choose the correct answer. [2 marks]

B. Justify your choice. [10 marks]

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
Problem 1

When a small elastic ball is released from some height above a smooth horizontal floor and falls freely, we expect it to rise back to its initial height after the elastic collision. With the following technique a small ball can behave like a “super ball”, bouncing back after the collision to a considerably greater height: from a point at height h, two small elastic balls with masses $m_1=3m$ and $m_2=m$ are released to fall simultaneously. The first collides head-on and elastically with the floor and, at the moment it leaves the floor, it collides again head-on and elastically with the second ball, which is coming down. After the collision, the ball of mass $m_2$ will shoot up to a height H equal to:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2024-1-fig1.png

(A) $3h$ (B) $4h$ (C) $5h$ (D) $6h$

Justify your answer.

problems.problem:
Problem 2

The spring (ideal) – mass system, with spring constant $k$ and a mass $M$, performs simple harmonic oscillation, as in the picture, above a motion sensor. The sensor measures the velocity of the mass $M$. In Experiment 1, $M=M_1=1.0\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $k=k_1$. In Experiment 2, $M=M_2=4.0\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $k=k_2$. The results of the two (2) experiments for one (1) period of the simple harmonic oscillations are given in the graph below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2024-2-fig1.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2024-2-fig2.png

The ratio $\dfrac{k_1}{k_2}$ is equal to:

(A) $\dfrac{1}{2}$ (B) $2$ (C) $\dfrac{1}{4}$ (D) $4$

Justify your answer.

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Problem 3

A homogeneous cylinder is wound with a thin, massless and inextensible string and is in equilibrium on the inclined plane, as shown in the figure. If the string AB is vertical and the angle of the inclined plane with the vertical direction is $\varphi$, then the ratio $\lambda$ of the tension of the string to the weight of the cylinder is given by the relation:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2024-3-fig1.png

(a) $\lambda=\dfrac{\cos\varphi}{1+\sin\varphi}$

(b) $\lambda=\dfrac{\cos\varphi}{1+\cos\varphi}$

(c) $\lambda=\dfrac{\sin\varphi}{1+\sin\varphi}$

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
Problem 4

The body Σ performs a vertical simple harmonic oscillation due to the rotational motion of the wheel T, which is converted into a reciprocating motion through the connection of the system with the rigid rod AB (that is, as the wheel T rotates, the body Σ moves up and down). The points A and B are freely rotating joints with negligible friction. On top of the body Σ we have placed a body of mass m. Let d be the distance of the centre of the wheel from the point where the rod AB is attached, and g the acceleration of gravity.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2024-4-fig1.png

Show that, for the body m not to lose contact with the body Σ, the angular velocity of the wheel must satisfy: $\omega<\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{d}}$.

problems.title: Problem 5
problems.problem:
Problem 5

The foundation of a building comprises a rectangular homogeneous slab made of concrete and steel reinforcement, embedded in the ground. The building comprises a self-contained structure which rests on the foundation not rigidly but with the possibility of sliding, with a coefficient of limiting (static) friction between them equal to $\mu=0.2$. A seismic event with period $T=1\,\mathrm{s}$ sets the system of the foundation together with the building into oscillation. The maximum amplitude of the oscillation for which the building does not slide on its base is equal to:

(A) $4\,\mathrm{cm}$ (B) $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ (C) $8\,\mathrm{cm}$ (D) $10\,\mathrm{cm}$

Justify your answer.

Given: $\pi^2\approx 10$ and $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2024-5-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 6
problems.problem:
Problem 6

A body of mass m moves with momentum of magnitude P and collides centrally and elastically with a stationary body of mass M. After the collision the initially stationary body acquires the maximum possible momentum. For the magnitude of the momentum acquired by the body of mass M and the relation between the masses it holds that:

(A) $P_M=1.25P$ and $M<m$

(B) $P_M=1.5P$ and $M>m$

(C) $P_M=3P$ and $M\ll m$

(D) $P_M=2P$ and $M\gg m$

Justify your answer.

problems.title: Problem 7
problems.problem:
Problem 7

On a smooth horizontal square table ΑΒΓΔ of side $\alpha=4\,\mathrm{m}$, standing at a great height, there are three small spheres $\Sigma_1$, $\Sigma_2$ and $\Sigma_3$ at rest, with masses m, 3m and 3m respectively. The sphere $\Sigma_1$ is tied to one end of a massless and inextensible string of length $\ell=\dfrac{\alpha}{2}=2\,\mathrm{m}$, the other end of which is tied immovably at the centre O of the table. The string can rotate without friction about the point O. The string is always taut. The sphere $\Sigma_2$ is at a point E of the side ΓΔ, while the sphere $\Sigma_3$ is at a point Z of the side ΑΓ. The straight segment OE is parallel to the side ΑΓ, while the straight segment OZ is parallel to the side ΓΔ. The string makes an angle $\theta=45^\circ$ with the straight segment OE. At time $t_0=0$ we give the body $\Sigma_1$ a velocity of magnitude $\upsilon=10\,\dfrac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}}$, with direction perpendicular to the string and sense towards the side ΓΔ, as shown in the figure. Calculate the distance between the spheres $\Sigma_2$ and $\Sigma_3$ at the moment when the body $\Sigma_3$ leaves the table.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2024-7-fig1.png

Top view

It is given that air resistance is negligible, $\pi=3.1$ and the magnitude of the acceleration of gravity is $g=10\,\dfrac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s^2}}$. All collisions of the bodies are to be considered central and elastic.

problems.title: Problem 1

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
A horizontal homogeneous beam has mass $m$, length $L$ and is in equilibrium on two vertical supports, $Y1$ and $Y2$, each of which is at a distance $L/4$ from the ends. At the middle of the beam an object of mass 3m is placed and is at rest. An internal explosion splits the object into two fragments $\Sigma1$ and $\Sigma2$ with masses $m_1, m_2$ respectively, and $m_2=2m_1$. The bodies $\Sigma1$ and $\Sigma2$ move without friction on the surface of the beam and head towards the supports $Y1$ and $Y2$ respectively.

(A) Find the relation between the forces $N_1, N_2$ exerted by the supports on $\Sigma1$ and $\Sigma2$ during their motion on the beam.

(B) Investigate whether the beam can overturn and show when this happens.

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Two small identical bodies, of mass m=1kg each, are fixed to the end of two identical ideal springs which have spring constant k=100 N/m and natural length $\ell_o=1m$. The free ends of the springs are fixed at the same fixed point O so that the springs have their natural length and their axes lie on the same horizontal straight line, which passes through the centres of mass of the bodies and through the point O, as shown in the figure. At some instant we release the two bodies, which then move in the same vertical plane. The two bodies arrive simultaneously at the lowest point of their curved trajectory, with horizontal velocities of magnitudes $u_1, u_2$, whereupon they collide head-on and inelastically (they stick together).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2025-3-fig1.png

1) Find the magnitude of the velocity of each body just before the collision, as well as the extension of each spring at that moment.

2) Show that the combined body, immediately after the collision, performs SHM (simple harmonic motion) and find its period.

3) Find the amplitude of the oscillation of the combined body and write the displacement–time equation, taking the downward direction as positive.

4) At the instant $t_1=\frac{T}{12}$ from the start of time (t=0), calculate the rates $\frac{\Delta k}{\Delta t}_{(t_1)}$ and $\frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}_{(t_1)}$. Also calculate the work of the resultant force $W_{\Sigma F}$ from the instant $\mathrm{t}=0$ to $t=t_1$.

5) Plot, on the same diagram, the graphs of the kinetic, the potential and the total energy of the oscillation as functions of time, with graduated axes, for the time interval $0\le t\le\frac{\pi}{2}\ s$.

Given: $g=10\,\frac{m}{s^2}$, $\sqrt{3}\cong 1{,}7$, $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=0{,}5$, $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\sqrt{18{,}75}\cong 4{,}33$. Resistances are considered negligible.

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
In the figure alongside, the square frame of side $\alpha=0{,}4\,m$ was made from a wire of length $\ell_{\sigma\upsilon\rho}=40\,m$ which has resistance per unit length $R^*=0{,}05\,\Omega/m$. The frame is in a magnetic field $B_1$, perpendicular to the field lines, with the magnitude of the magnetic field varying with time according to the relation $B_1=2{,}5t$ (S.I). The electrical source has emf $E=8\,V$ and internal resistance r. A resistor has ohmic resistance $R_1=12\,\Omega$. A horizontally placed rod of length (ΚΛ)=1m and resistance $R_2=4\,\Omega$ is constantly in contact with the vertical wires (of negligible resistance). The rod is in a uniform magnetic field with $B_2=2\,T$, perpendicular to the field lines. Initially all the switches are open. At the instant t=0 we close the switch $\delta_1$ and observe that the rod is in equilibrium. The magnitude of the acceleration of gravity is given, g=10 m/s$^2$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2025-4-fig1.png

[Label in the figure: μονωτικό δάπεδο = insulating floor.]

A) Calculate the direction of B$_1$, the direction of B$_2$ and the mass of the rod, if you know that the conventional direction of the current flowing in the frame is anticlockwise (opposite to the direction of rotation of the hands of a clock) and in the rod it is directed from Κ to Λ. At some instant we open the switch δ$_1$ and at the same time close the switch δ$_2$. We observe that the rod continues to be in equilibrium.

B) Find the internal resistance of the source.

At some later instant we open the switch δ$_2$ and the rod starts to descend, remaining all the time inside the magnetic field of magnitude B$_2$.

C) Calculate the maximum electric power in the resistor R$_1$.

While the rod has acquired its terminal velocity, we close the switch δ$_3$.

D) Calculate the magnitude of the rate of change of the electric current in the coil at the instant we close the switch δ$_3$. Given $\mu_o=4\pi10^{-7}\,Tm/A$, $R_3=12\,\Omega$ and, for the ideal coil: length $\ell_\pi=20\pi\,cm$, cross-sectional area of one turn $A_\pi=0{,}1\,m^2$ and N$_\pi$=10$^3$ turns.

E) Calculate the maximum value of the energy of the magnetic field of the coil.

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
A homogeneous rod of weight $w_0$ is bent so that its unequal legs form an acute angle equal to $\varphi$. The lengths of the two legs have ratio equal to $\lambda > 1$. The "angle" is hung from its vertex on a nail without friction and is left to come to equilibrium in a vertical plane, freely under its own weight.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-1-fig1.png

(a) Find, in this position, the angle between the bisector of the angle $\varphi$ and the vertical direction.

(b) With a weight of weight $w$ hung by a string at one of the two ends of the rod, the "angle" rotates so that in the new equilibrium each leg forms the same angle $\theta$ with the horizontal direction. Show that $\dfrac{w}{w_0}=\dfrac{\lambda-1}{2}$.

Given: $\cos(90-A)=\sin A$, $\sin(A\pm B)=\sin A\cos B\pm\sin B\cos A$.

[2×8 marks]

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
In the circuit of the figure, the electrical sources have emf equal to $E$ and negligible internal resistance, and the coil has self-inductance $L$ and negligible ohmic resistance, while for the resistances $R_1=2R$ and $R_2=R$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-fig1.png

Initially the switch δ is open and a steady value of the current has been established.
